messages.text: :siren: P1: ECS tasks for the main Spring Boot app are crash-looping with OOMKilled.
Looking into Datadog now. CPU is normal but memory spiked right before the crash.
I pulled a heap dump from the last running task. Retained size on the response cache is 1.8GB — the LRU eviction isn't firing.
Confirmed: the cache TTL was accidentally set to Duration.ZERO in the last deploy, so entries never expire.
Resolution: Reverted the cache TTL change and scaled ECS memory from 2GB to 4GB as a safety buffer. Stable now. Next action: Profile the heap dump tomorrow to right-size the memory limit.
:siren: P2: Huge spike in the SQS Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) for payment processing.
DLQ is at 12k messages. Sampling a few — they all fail JSON parsing on the `refund_reason` field.
The upstream team started sending `refund_reason: null` last night. Our consumer's Jackson config rejects nulls on that field.
Patched the consumer to treat null as empty string and redeployed.
Mitigation: Flushed the SQS DLQ back to the main queue after fixing the parsing bug in the consumer. DLQ is draining at ~200/s.
:siren: P1: API Gateway is returning 502s for the checkout endpoint.
Started ~15 min ago. Correlated with the API Gateway integration timeout config change we pushed at 14:02.
Reverted the timeout change back to 29s. Still seeing 502s.
The underlying Lambda is timing out at 30s now — the API Gateway revert didn't help because the Lambda itself was also changed.
Pending: Reverted the API Gateway config, but we are still seeing 502s. Escalating to AWS support and rolling back the Lambda deployment as well.
:siren: P3: HikariCP connection pool timeout exceptions in the user service.
Pool size is 20, active connections 20 — pool is saturated. Checking slow query log.
Found it: the new `getUserSessions` query is doing a full table scan on `sessions` because we forgot the index on `user_id`.
Adding the index now with CONCURRENTLY so we don't lock the table.
Resolution: Added btree index on sessions(user_id). Query latency dropped from 4s to 8ms. Pool utilization back to <20%.
:siren: P2: Thundering herd effect observed on the cache cluster after the Redis restart.
All services fired their cache-miss fallback simultaneously. DB CPU pegged at 100%.
Root cause is that our clients have zero jitter on cache reconnect — they all hit the DB in the same 200ms window.
Resolution: Added exponential backoff with jitter (0-500ms) to our retry logic to prevent the thundering herd. DB CPU is dropping. Deployed to all services.
:siren: P2: Lambda timeouts on the third-party webhook handler.
The webhook forwards to Stripe's API. Stripe is showing degraded status on their status page.
Our Lambda timeout is 10s but Stripe is taking 12-14s to respond right now.
Pending: Increased Lambda timeout to 15s as a band-aid. We need to make this handler async (SQS-backed) tomorrow so we don't block on Stripe.
:siren: P3: S3 Access Denied errors when the new reporting cron tries to upload PDFs.
The cron runs as the `reporting-task` ECS task role. Checking the attached IAM policy.
The IAM role for the ECS task is missing `s3:PutObject` on the `reports-prod` bucket. It only has `s3:GetObject`.
Resolution: Attached the correct IAM policy granting s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::reports-prod/*. Uploads are working.
:siren: P2: Internal service-to-service TLS handshake failing with 'certificate expired'.
The internal CA cert for the `orders` service expired at 00:00 UTC. Renewal cron didn't fire.
The renewal cron was tied to the old Jenkins job that we decommissioned last month. No one migrated it.
Resolution: Manually rotated the cert via cert-manager and set up a new K8s CronJob for renewals. Added a Datadog monitor for cert expiry <14 days.
:siren: P1: Post-deploy NullPointerException on the checkout confirmation page.
The new PromotionService returns null when no promo applies, but the caller assumes an empty Optional.
Rolling back deployment v2.14.3 to v2.14.2 now.
Resolution: Rolled back the deployment. Fix PR is up to make PromotionService return Optional.empty() instead of null. Will redeploy after review.
:siren: P2: RDS primary failed over to a different AZ unexpectedly.
AWS Health Dashboard shows scheduled maintenance in us-east-1a. Our primary was in that AZ.
Replica in us-east-1b was promoted. Seeing ~30s of connection errors during the flip.
Resolution: Failover completed cleanly. Reviewed our HikariCP config — reduced `maxLifetime` to 30 min so connections rotate more often and pick up DNS changes faster.
:siren: P2: Kafka consumer lag on the analytics pipeline growing at 5k msg/min.
Consumer group rebalance is happening every 90s — one consumer keeps getting kicked.
The kicked consumer's session timeout is hitting because a downstream ClickHouse write is taking 45s.
Resolution: Increased Kafka `session.timeout.ms` from 30s to 60s and added batch flushing to the ClickHouse writer. Lag draining at 8k/min.
:siren: P3: Prometheus scrapes failing for all pods in the `payments` namespace.
Prometheus can't reach the pod IPs. Testing from the Prometheus pod: connection refused.
New NetworkPolicy was applied to `payments` yesterday that only allows ingress from `frontend` namespace. Prometheus is in `monitoring`.
Resolution: Updated the NetworkPolicy to also allow ingress from the `monitoring` namespace on the metrics port. Scrapes recovered.
:siren: P2: Users seeing stale JavaScript bundle after the frontend deploy.
CloudFront is serving the old `main.abc123.js` — cache TTL is set to 1 year on the bundle.
That's expected for hashed assets, but the `index.html` also has 1 year TTL, so browsers never fetch the new bundle name.
Resolution: Set Cache-Control: no-cache on index.html in the CloudFront behavior. Invalidated /index.html. Users will pick up new bundles on next page load.
:siren: P2: DynamoDB throttling on the `sessions` table, ~2% of reads failing.
CloudWatch shows one partition getting 80% of the traffic. Classic hot partition.
The partition key is `tenant_id` — one enterprise customer accounts for 60% of active sessions.
Pending: Adding a suffix (`tenant_id#shard_N` where N = hash(session_id) % 10) to spread writes. Migration will happen this weekend during the low-traffic window.
:siren: P2: Nginx ingress returning 504 Gateway Timeout for /api/reports endpoint.
The reports endpoint generates PDFs and can take 45s. Nginx ingress default timeout is 60s but I'm seeing 504s at exactly 30s.
Found it — the ingress has `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout: "30"` in its annotations from a copy-paste from another service.
Resolution: Bumped proxy-read-timeout to 90s for the /api/reports path. Long-term: move PDF generation to an async job queue so the HTTP request returns immediately.
:siren: P3: JVM GC pauses of 3-5s observed on the recommendations service.
G1GC logs show Full GC events triggered by humongous allocations. Something is allocating >12MB objects (region size is 24MB / 2).
The new recommendation model loads a 40MB feature array into a single ByteBuffer on every request.
Resolution: Moved the feature array to a shared static field (loaded once at startup). Full GC events dropped to zero. P99 latency down from 800ms to 60ms.
